content.text:
**Finding: compliant — no redline proposed.**

The TRANSITION rule is satisfied by a combination of clauses, and importantly the data limb runs in our favour:

- **Data return / certified deletion — Section 9.7 (p0517–p0518).** Termination-triggered, mutual, and exercisable at the *requesting* Party's written election: either destroy all copies and *confirm destruction in writing*, or deliver all copies back. Retention is capped at one archival/legal copy plus automated back-ups. That is essentially the preferred "return, then delete and certify" construct, enforceable by us against Harpoon.
- **Transition / wind-down —** Article 12.7 and Section 12.6.1(c) (reversion mechanics and data/Regulatory Documentation transfer), the post-termination sell-off period in Section 12.10.2, and surviving Section 3.8.5 (p0331), which preserves Harpoon's record retention and our right to copies after termination.
- **"Help moving" is already ours** under Sections 3.5, 3.8.2(a) and 4.5.2 — full Manufacturing Technology Transfer with reasonable assistance, continuing at our request against reimbursement.

Direction check: the exit transfer/destruction duties in Article 12.7 bind AbbVie, not Harpoon, because rights in the Licensed Compounds revert to Harpoon on termination. That is inherent in the option/licence bargain rather than a vendor-side gap, and a Vendor data-return insert would be inapposite — Harpoon holds no AbbVie service data as a processor.

Noted in the rationale but not flagged as deviations: Section 9.7 says "as soon as reasonably practicable" rather than a fixed 30-day window and specifies no machine-readable format; and Section 12.6.1(c) permits Harpoon to elect destruction of AbbVie-generated data (mitigated by the Section 12.10.2 sell-off right and the retained archival copy under 9.7). These are minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording, so the clause set sits at or above the fallback.
